title: Speed to lead and the 3 strikes

steps.text: Maria sees a home online. She taps "Contact agent". Her phone is still in her hand. How fast should you call?

steps.q: How fast do you call a new lead?
steps.why: 180 seconds is 3 minutes. She is still thinking about the home.

steps.sub: The first helpful call usually wins.

steps.text: A call in 5 minutes beats a call in 30 minutes. Your chance is about **21 times better**.

steps.before: A call in 5 minutes is about

steps.h: Why does speed win? Tap each card

cards.back: Maybe. The first helpful call usually wins.

cards.front: You are writing a note. A lead comes in.
cards.back: Stop and dial. Only finish a live call first.

steps.text: Call **9 AM to 8 PM**, Monday to Saturday. On Sunday, **noon to 8 PM**. Use the **lead's** time, not yours. Texts follow the same window.

steps.h: This is the lead's time. Call now?

steps.q: A lead comes in at 10:40 PM their time. What do you do?
options: Call at 9 AM tomorrow, before any other call
Send a text now. It is only a text.
Call now, but keep it short
steps.why: No calls or texts after 8 PM. Call first when the window opens.

steps.text: The calling window always beats speed.
steps.sub: Follow the rules first. Then be fast.

steps.text: Most leads do not answer the first call. They are at work or driving. So you use **3 strikes**. A strike is one try.

cards.back: Call now. Let it ring 5 to 6 times. Leave a 20-second voicemail.
Text at 2 minutes. Only if they agreed to texts.
Call again about 4 hours later, before 6 PM their time.

items: Call and leave a short voicemail

steps.line: Hi Maria, this is Ana with Rivera Home Team. You asked about 12 Oak Street. I will try you again soon.

options: Hi Maria, it's Ana with Rivera Home Team. I called about 12 Oak Street. Want to see it Thursday at 5 or Saturday at 11?
steps.why: It says her name, the home, and two times.

steps.q: Maria did not agree to texts. What is Strike 2?
options: Skip the text. Set the Strike 3 call.
steps.why: Text only leads who agreed to texts.

steps.q: A lead comes in Tuesday at 6:30 PM. No answer. When is Strike 3?
steps.why: Four hours later is too late. Call first when the window opens.

steps.text: If the lead answers or texts back, the strikes stop. Now you talk and offer a time. **Log every try** in Follow Up Boss.

steps.says: Hi! Is 12 Oak Street still for sale?

options.text: Yes! And the price can go lower.
options.why: Never guess. Never talk about price.

options.text: I will ask Daniel, our agent, now. Want to see it Thursday at 5 or Saturday at 11?
options.why: Honest, fast, and it offers two times.

options.text: I will get back to you next week.
options.why: Too slow. She will find another agent.

steps.q: What is your goal in the first 3 minutes?
options: Wait to see if the lead calls you
Call fast, learn what they want, and set an appointment
steps.why: Call fast. Learn what they want. Book a time with the agent.

steps.q: Three strikes and still no answer. Is the lead lost?
options: No. Log all 3 tries. Follow-up keeps going.
steps.why: Many leads answer later. Never delete a lead for no answer.

steps.sub: Many people read texts but skip calls.

steps.text: You did it! You can now call fast and run the 3 strikes.

quiz.q: A new lead comes in at 2 PM their time. When do you call?
options: At the end of your shift
quiz.explain: Call in 180 seconds, inside the calling window.

quiz.q: A call in 5 minutes, not 30, makes your chance about:
quiz.explain: Fast calls are about 21 times better.

quiz.q: The lead does not answer your first call. What is next?
options: Leave a voicemail, then text at 2 minutes
quiz.explain: Strike 2 is a text, if they agreed to texts.

quiz.q: A lead comes in at 9:30 PM their time. What do you do?
options: Call first when the window opens
quiz.explain: No calls or texts after 8 PM their time.

quiz.q: What is your goal in the first 3 minutes?
options: Call fast, learn what they want, set an appointment
Wait for the lead to call
quiz.explain: Speed, then questions, then an appointment.
